editorial:
You follow Alice as a 19-year-old who tumbles back down the rabbit hole into a world she barely remembers. This time, Wonderland is darker and stranger, and the creatures need her help to stop the Red Queen's rule. Johnny Depp plays the Mad Hatter with wild energy, while Helena Bonham Carter steals scenes as the big-headed Red Queen. The whole movie feels like a dream you cannot quite shake, full of talking animals, giant mushrooms, and battles that feel bigger than a fairy tale should. Tim Burton's style is everywhere, from the twisted trees to the oddball costumes, so if you like his other movies, you will feel right at home.

The acting is fun, especially Depp and Bonham Carter, and the action picks up in the second half with a big dragon fight. The pacing drags a little early on, and the story can feel thin if you want deep meaning. Still, the visuals are gorgeous and worth seeing on a big screen. Families with older kids and fantasy fans will enjoy it most. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alice faces the Jabberwocky in a giant battle and defeats it, breaking the Red Queen's power. The White Queen takes back the throne, and Alice chooses to return home. She turns down a marriage proposal and decides to travel the world on her own terms, using what she learned in Wonderland to find her own path. The twist is that Wonderland was always meant to push her toward real-life courage.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves fantasy adventures with quirky characters and big visuals.
